newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian braodcaster sale on hold - analyst says.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian braodcaster sale on hold - analyst says.

text.p: The privatisation of Hungary's state broadcaster Antenna Hungaria Rt will probably remain undecided until late next year, an analyst said on Tuesday.
Media analyst Attila Ledenyi said the fate of the sale was unlikely to be raised again until the sell-off of Hungary's media was settled late in 1997.
Antenna Hungaria transmits all Hungary's national TV and radio programmes.

"A compromise was made a couple of months ago within the government not to deal with Antenna Hungaria until after the radio and TV frequencies are given out," Ledenyi said. "That means not until at least the second half of 1997."
Prime Minister Gyula Horn said last week the government had no plans to privatise Antenna Hungaria, which transmits all Hungarian national television and radio programmes.
"Privatising Antenna Hungaria is not on the government's agenda," Horn told reporters.
The privatisation involves a second state channel and a third channel. Two national radio frequencies are also available.

Hungary's media law, passed last December after four years of political dispute, stipulates that 10-year concessions for the two television channels should be put out to tender in time for the new channels to be launched on January 1.
But government policy changes and uncertainties over Antenna Hungaria, which will upgrade the third frequency for national broadcasting, have caused the process to fall behind schedule.

The strongest opposition to the sale of Antenna Hungaria, which is owed 2.5 billion forints ($15.7 million) in unpaid broadcasting fees, comes from chairman of national broadcasting authority ORTT, Mihaly Revesz. ORTT is overseeing the media privatisation.
Revesz, a close ally of premier Horn, is opposed to broadcasting equipment or the channels themselves falling into foreign ownership.
Such is Revesz's political sway he could kill the sell-off all together, analyst Ledenyi said. "The story may be over but...they haven't made it public," he said.
The government is bound by a March decree to privatise Antenna Hungaria and faces a battle with coalition partners, the Free Democrats who favour the sale, if it cancels the law.

France's Tele Diffusion de France (TDF) was the only bidder when state privatisation agency APV offered its 50 percent plus one share stake in Antenna Hungaria in June. The bid, which was well below the 8.4 billion forint asking price, was turned down.
Jean-Francois Fenech, TDF business development manager, said the group remained interested in Antenna Hungaria but was waiting for clarification of the government's real intent.
"We are still interested because we have been cooperating with the firm for five years -- but under reasonable conditions," Fenech said.
GTS Hungary, a subsidiary of U.S. group Global TeleSystems, was also rumoured to be considering a bid in a new tender.
"We were not really ready for the first tender but we would have been interested in the conditions for the second," GTS's managing director Istvan Pesti told reporters last week.
But, he said, he was not very hopeful that such a tender would take place. "If you ask me I don't believe the company is going to be privatised in the near future," Pesti said. ($1=158.93 Forint)
